title: Sent to the Board without a recommendation
question: When a committee declines to recommend a money file, what does the Board then do with it?
finding: Committees sent 67 money files to the Board without a recommendation or, once, with a recommendation of “do not pass”. 62 reached a recorded Board vote: 47 passed with no dissent, 13 passed over at least one no and 2 were voted down. That is a no vote on 24.2% of them, against 3.2% for all other money files (chance alone would give a gap that wide less than 1% of the time). 5 never reached a recorded Board vote. The one “do not pass” file, an office lease, was then voted down by all eleven members.
how: Every committee roll call on a money file whose action is “referred without recommendation” (in any of its printed forms) or “recommended ‘do not pass’”, with the Board’s final vote on the same file. Files the Board voted down come first, then those passed over a no (closest first), those with no recorded Board vote, and those passed with no dissent, largest title amount first. The link opens the Board’s vote page where there is one, or the minutes where the vote was read from them.
limits: Sending a file on without a recommendation is one of the three courses the rules give a committee, and the committee votes shown here were themselves almost all unanimous: it can mean the members wanted the full Board to decide, or that time was short. A file filed or still pending afterwards may simply have been replaced by another. Parties that are private persons are not named. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
